description:
The verify_* functions return Result<(), IdentityError>. On Ok, the caller learns 'a SAN entry matched' but not *which* one (e.g., 'matched wildcard *.foo.com', 'matched IP 192.0.2.1', 'matched rfc822Name vs SmtpUTF8Mailbox').

Caller impact:

* TLS server-name validators that log 'cert vended for example.com via *.example.com wildcard' have to walk the SAN themselves *after* a successful match.
* Audit / compliance reports needing to record the matched SAN entry pay 2x SAN parse cost.
* Wildcard-vs-exact telemetry (security teams want to know how often wildcard matches occur in their fleet) requires a second pass.

The signature `Result<(), IdentityError>` is the simplest shape but it's a one-way commitment. Once shipped, the maintainer cannot change the Ok variant to carry data without breaking every existing caller.

Lower-friction alternatives — all chosen before 1.0 because the Ok shape is immutable post-ship:

1. Return Result<MatchInfo, IdentityError> where MatchInfo is #[non_exhaustive] and carries which-entry-matched info. This is the most correct shape.

2. Provide a second function verify_dns_name_with_info that returns the rich variant; keep the simple one as a wrapper. Doubles surface area.

3. Pass a &mut Option<MatchInfo> out-param. Ugly; not idiomatic.

4. Add a 'last match' accessor on ServerName. Stateful; thread-hostile.

5. Document the loss explicitly. Punts the problem to callers forever.

Best option: (1). The shape:

  pub struct DnsMatch<'a> {
      pub matched_san: &'a str,
      pub via_wildcard: bool,
  }
  pub fn verify_dns_name(...) -> Result<DnsMatch<'_>, IdentityError>;

(non_exhaustive, lifetime tied to cert).

For verify_mailbox similarly: which SAN form matched (Rfc822Name vs SmtpUTF8Mailbox).

Severity P2 (was P1, downgraded): callers can subset with `let _ = verify_dns_name(..)?;` if they don't want the info, so this is largely additive. The bar for changing the signature later is high though — file this as a 1.0-blocker design decision.
title: verify_dns_name / verify_mailbox discard which SAN entry matched — diagnostic info lost forever
